why_points: The date can be wrong while labelled verified: one stored deadline was a registration date, and 12 of 39 stored deadlines read 'verified' on call status alone, not on the date.
Everything else we collect (organiser, sponsorship, categories, overview, about 24 fields) arrives at varying quality, from different sources, and none of it has been measured.

The weekend research fails about 73% of its Gemini calls, September cost $134, and weeks of building still need manual rescue.

items.r: Standing process, agreed 10-03. Measure it: the share of events that needed a manual verification each month should fall. A pin holds one edition; next year's edition is a new row, so the rules (steps 3-5) are what make manual checks rarer.

quality.split_method: COMPLETE % = expected fields that are filled (a pinned honest blank counts as filled) averaged with coverage of customer-tracked events. Edition facts (start date, city, country, main page) are always expected; the call fields (deadline, link, evidence) are excused while the event starts more than 90 days ahead and no call is open, because nothing is published yet. ACCURATE % = proven / (proven + contradicted) over facts we state (deadline vs its cited page, start year vs edition, pinned facts, customer-verified dates, spot checks); unproven is shown beside it and never counted wrong; a contradiction is never excused by the 90-day rule. Awards have no event start, so no grace applies.
